sampling_model.design: Two-arm baseline randomized trial with fixed switch time \(k\), terminal horizon \(K\), and no observed cross-arm switching.
sampling_model.units: Independent trial participants with fixed finite recurrent-event and death histories under the superpopulation law \(\mathsf P\).
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline assignment \(R\in\{0,1\}\); candidate regimes retain intensive treatment before \(k\) and switch survivors with \(B\ge m\) to standard treatment.
sampling_model.overlap: The maintained class assumes positive baseline assignment and positive arm-specific factual censoring continuation on every supported at-risk history, with no positivity for the unsupported switch. The positive inference submodel separately fixes \(H\), \(K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\) and requires assignment, landmark survival, and every supported factual continuation probability to be at least \(\varepsilon\); the base class itself is unchanged.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Every sustained-history atom is identified by a proved product of observed at-risk transition kernels. The finite cell vector is estimated by cross-fitted longitudinal AIPW scores for intensive cell indicators and by numerator, survival-denominator, and ratio scores for the standard residual margin. Clipped, uniformly consistent backward-regression and censoring-hazard fits with \(o_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\) regression--censoring error products yield a root-\(n\) simultaneous rectangle on the quantitative submodel. Hall-feasible projection keeps its confidence polytope nonempty. Under pointwise overlap alone, the vanishing-information impossibility still applies.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Assumption 1 supplies the published uncapped residual no-carry-over equality, Proposition 1 supplies threshold-wise scalar bounds, and the decision section compares deterministic switching regimes.

The paper characterizes atom-sensitive sharp bounds for the distribution of an unrestricted sum with fixed marginals.

body.tldr: A randomized recurrent-event trial identifies separately capped baseline and residual margins while leaving their dependence unknown, and the raw recurrent paths remain unbounded. The externally prespecified sensitivity restriction \(B+W\le H\) creates a Ferrers transport problem and is not implied by separate capping. The cap-fibre response-tree construction proves every feasible triple coupling attainable, including in the published raw no-carry-over subclass. Exact endpoints and the common-law value polytope yield deterministic and randomized minimax regret and the cap-three recommendation reversal. For inference, a direct sequential-factorization proof now identifies every supported sustained-history atom and hence \((r_{bt},q_w)\); on the explicit quantitative-overlap and cross-fitted product-rate submodel, a longitudinal AIPW Bonferroni rectangle contracts at root-\(n\) rate and its perspective inversion covers the whole value set and every deterministic or randomized robust optimizer, including ties. On the broader pointwise-overlap class \(\mathfrak M_H\), uniformly shrinking inference remains impossible by the vanishing-information two-law construction. Thus the positive quantitative theorem and the negative base-class theorem have disjoint, explicit scopes.

project_justification.gap: The closest recurrent-event switching analysis supplies an uncapped no-carry-over equality, scalar sharp bounds, and deterministic decision criteria. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 supplies the factual-arm sequential-CAR setup and influence-function architecture for recurrent-event mean and survival targets, but not an atom-by-atom identification theorem for the complete sustained history, the capped margin vector used here, shared-law deterministic and randomized regret inversion, or the positive-versus-negative uniform-inference boundary. Dahl2008 supplies staircase feasibility only.
project_justification.niche: An externally prespecified joint-capacity sensitivity restriction on two separately capped summaries creates nested antidiagonal support without globally bounding the underlying recurrent-event paths. The attributed staircase feasibility result in Dahl2008, Theorem 4, then becomes an input to a causal sharpness and joint-decision problem rather than the source of novelty.
project_justification.fill: The formal kernel combines the attributed staircase feasibility certificate with an explicit raw-path cap-fibre lift, derives the complete common-law value and regret geometry, and proves the missing inference chain. Sequential CAR and positivity give a finite product of observed transition kernels for every supported absorbing history atom. Explicit backward regressions, cumulative censoring hazards, longitudinal AIPW and ratio influence functions, cross-fitting, Hall-feasible projection, and conservative simultaneous inversion give root-\(n\) value-set and regret-excess contraction on a quantitative regularity submodel. A separate two-law theorem proves that pointwise positivity in the unchanged base class cannot yield uniform shrinkage.

body.related_work: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 supplies the uncapped residual no-carry-over equality and threshold-wise scalar analysis. The cap-fibre construction here transfers sharpness after intersecting that class with \(B+W\le H\). Dahl2008 supplies the reindexed staircase feasibility criterion, and Hoffman1952 supplies only the fixed-matrix polyhedral error bound used for the new perspective-Lipschitz argument. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 is used for the factual-arm sequential-CAR formulation and motivates longitudinal influence-function estimation; it does not assert identification of the entire sustained-history law. That law is derived here atom by atom from randomization, consistency, sequential CAR, and positivity, then specialized to \(r_{bt}\) and the numerator--denominator representation of \(q_w\). ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, AndrewsSoares2010, and Gafarov2025 motivate inference with binding inequalities and changing faces. The present positive result is a finite-dimensional conservative cross-fitted inversion under quantitative overlap, while the headline two-point theorem shows why the same conclusion is impossible uniformly under pointwise overlap. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 motivates the decision relevance of the shared payoff set and randomization.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The cap \(H\) constrains only the separately capped summaries and never the primitive raw recurrent counts. Its clinical mechanism is not established for SPRINT. The response-tree lift preserves factual-arm sequential censoring without assuming censoring independence from the whole response tree. The positive inference theorem is not a consequence of the maintained class: it uses a separate quantitative predicate with uniform assignment, survival, and factual censoring overlap and explicit nuisance product rates. The conservative Bonferroni--Chebyshev rectangle establishes uniform root-\(n\) order but does not claim semiparametric efficiency or shortest width. At Hall and policy ties, outer coverage and regret-excess contraction remain valid, but optimizer-set distance need not contract without the displayed gap or polyhedral-sharpness condition. The broad-class impossibility sequences violate every fixed quantitative overlap bound and therefore do not contradict the positive submodel theorem.
body.honest_scope: The proved scope includes exact endpoints, an observed-law-preserving raw-path causal lift, sharp transfer to the published raw no-carry-over subclass intersected with the cap, the complete common-law value set, deterministic and randomized minimax regret, and confidence-polytope inversion. Complete sustained-arm history identification is now proved directly by a finite observed-kernel product, rather than attributed to a source that identifies only particular functionals. Positive root-\(n\) margin, value-set, and regret-excess contraction holds only on the explicit quantitative inference regularity submodel with fixed \(H,K\), a fixed overlap lower bound, cross-fitting, clipped uniformly consistent nuisances, and longitudinal product-rate control. All deterministic and randomized ties retain simultaneous outer coverage. Geometric optimizer contraction is claimed only under an additional uniform deterministic regret gap or randomized polyhedral-sharpness inequality. On the unchanged pointwise-overlap class, uniformly honest regions need not shrink, as witnessed by the stated two-law sequences. SPRINT remains only a conditional capped-loss consumer requiring an externally defended cap at \(k=300\) and a feasible censoring-adjusted Hall system.
